sn56.15:1.1: “Bhikkhus, do you remember the Four Noble Truths taught by me?”
sn56.15:1.2: When this was said, a certain bhikkhu said to the Blessed One:
sn56.15:1.3: “Venerable sir, I remember the Four Noble Truths taught by the Blessed One.”
sn56.15:1.5: do you remember the Four Noble Truths taught by me?” “I remember suffering, venerable sir, as the first noble truth taught by the Blessed One.
sn56.15:1.6: I remember the origin of suffering as the second noble truth taught by the Blessed One.
sn56.15:1.7: I remember the cessation of suffering as the third noble truth taught by the Blessed One.
sn56.15:1.8: I remember the way leading to the cessation of suffering as the fourth noble truth taught by the Blessed One. It is in this way,
sn56.15:1.9: venerable sir, that I remember the Four Noble Truths taught by the Blessed One.”
sn56.15:2.2: It is good that you remember the Four Noble Truths taught by me.
sn56.15:2.3: Suffering, bhikkhu, is the first noble truth taught by me: remember it thus.
sn56.15:2.4: The origin of suffering is the second noble truth taught by me: remember it thus.
sn56.15:2.5: The cessation of suffering is the third noble truth taught by me: remember it thus.
sn56.15:2.6: The way leading to the cessation of suffering is the fourth noble truth taught by me: remember it thus.
sn56.15:2.7: In this way, bhikkhu, remember the Four Noble Truths taught by me.
sn56.15:3.1: “Therefore, bhikkhu, an exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is suffering.’… An exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.’”
